  1. Installation

Installation

Prerequisites

Requirement Detail
Kubernetes 1.30 or later
Helm 3.19 or later
cert-manager Required by the KServe controller webhooks
Gateway API CRDs Required when you use Gateway-based routing or LLMInferenceService routers
GPU device plugin Required for any GPU workload, for example the NVIDIA device plugin
LeaderWorkerSet Required only for multi-node LLMInferenceService workloads

Check cert-manager before installing:

kubectl get pods -n cert-manager
kubectl get crd certificates.cert-manager.io

Namespaces

This chart uses two distinct namespaces.

Namespace Purpose Controlled by
Release namespace KServe controllers, webhooks, and shared configuration helm --namespace
Workload namespace Your InferenceService and LLMInferenceService objects namespace value

Install the controllers into kserve. KServe v0.20.0 contains namespace-sensitive webhook and cert-manager references, so a different release namespace is not supported.

# values.yaml
namespace: models

helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve --create-namespace \
  -f values.yaml

Create the workload namespace yourself; the chart does not create it:

kubectl create namespace models

Install from source 

helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving
helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve --create-namespace \
  -f my-values.yaml

helm dependency build downloads the seven pinned KServe charts listed in Chart.lock. Run it after every clone and after any dependency change.

Install from the registry 

helm upgrade --install model-serving \
  oci://ghcr.io/sassoftware/sas-retrieval-agent-manager-examples/model-serving \
  --version 0.1.0 \
  --namespace kserve --create-namespace \
  -f my-values.yaml

Published chart versions are immutable. Pin --version in every environment.

Verify the installation 

helm status model-serving -n kserve
kubectl get pods -n kserve
kubectl get clusterservingruntime
kubectl get inferenceservice -n models
kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models

A healthy controller namespace shows running kserve-controller-manager and, when enabled, llmisvc-controller-manager pods.

Preview the rendered manifests

Always review before applying to a shared cluster:

helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve --include-crds -f my-values.yaml > rendered.yaml

Upgrade 

helm dependency build helm-charts/model-serving
helm upgrade model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve -f my-values.yaml

Adding or removing entries in models and llmInferenceServices is a normal upgrade. Removing an entry deletes the corresponding workload.

Uninstall 

helm uninstall model-serving -n kserve

Helm does not delete CRDs on uninstall. Custom resources such as InferenceService remain registered cluster-wide. Deleting the CRDs deletes every model object in every namespace.

To remove the CRDs deliberately:

kubectl get crd | grep kserve.io
kubectl delete crd inferenceservices.serving.kserve.io

CRD lifecycle and existing KServe installations

Helm applies subchart CRDs before templates. If KServe is already installed by another release or by kubectl apply, the cluster-scoped CRDs, webhooks, and cluster roles already have an owner and this install will conflict.

Before installing into such a cluster:

  1. List existing owners: helm list -A | grep -i kserve.
  2. Remove the previous installation, or disable the overlapping components with components.*.enabled: false.
  3. Confirm no leftover webhooks remain: kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration | grep kserve.

See Components for selectively disabling parts of KServe.
